items.reasons: Rule 3 first: neither return states anything the installed client, repository or sources contradict. A's statements hold: the client says /mcp and /context cannot be invoked via the Skill tool and tells the model to ask the user to run them (C1, C2); the repository uses them inside an interactive session (recipes/claude-native-profile.md:272-273); ToolSearch loads deferred MCP tools (T2, R49). B's statements hold: /plugin is real in the interactive client (R48, CHANGELOG 2.1.275, which the repository ranks above docs per docs/harness-defaults.md:58; R10, R43), the Skill tool exposes only some built-in commands (R5), and plugins include agents (T1). The current line (CLAUDE.md:3-4) tells the model to use /mcp and /context, which C1 and C2 show it cannot invoke, so 'neither' is not warranted. Executed comparison (headless claude -p per comparison_method; host's default model only): A and B tie on the primary and secondary metrics (correct 9/9, answered 9/9, no_builtin_skill 9/9). They also match on the descriptive loaded_schema (9, 9; current line 5) and executed_target (6, 6; current line 3), which the packet counts as behavior, not better or worse. asks_user was 0 in all 36 runs, question_only was 0 in all 9 K4 runs, and K4's premise did not hold. So the fallback on which A and B differ was never exercised, and the decision below is reasoning from sources, not a measured result. Decisive point, Rule 4's 'interactive and headless': the line is read in headless runs (the claude -p comparison's loaded_schema changed with the CLAUDE.md text) and in this repository's workflow agent() stages (AGENTS.md:36), where no user may answer (round_1_points[0]). A's fallback (report it as unconfirmed and name the command that would) gives a status in a headless run and still tells an interactive user which command to run. It fits AGENTS.md:15 (recorded limitations are context; stop only for sign-in, OS consent or an unresolved material decision), R63 (sample prompt: say exactly what you left out and why) and R50 (evidence that works for sessions you weren't watching). B's fallback (ask for the relevant /plugin, /mcp or /context output) suits interactive sessions but leaves an unattended run or workflow child with a request no one may be present to act on. R7 lets a -p caller type /mcp, but that is a separate run. That its summary would reflect the asking session is inference, and NF3 records no source showing that claude mcp list run from inside a session reports that session's connections. Counter-evidence weighed: C1, C2 and R15 show the client's own pattern is to ask the user, and R61 supports pausing for input only the user can provide; A's named command keeps that path open without blocking. On /plugin, B is not contradicted, but the reference adds little for 'active in this session': it is absent from the headless command list (C4), its list reports settings enablement and load errors (R43, R44), and a plugin can be installed without being activated in the session (R45). A names the two commands R42 documents for the current session's context and each server's connection status. Coverage favors B in principle: it covers agents (T1), and listed tool names are not proof of a live server (R27, R29), matching the repository's own practice of making one useful call (docs/token-session-handbook.md:67). Coverage does not decide the case: A's text, with no execute instruction, matched B on executed_target (6 vs 6) and correct, and its K3 runs report a read-only call to every server with tools (comparison_k1_k3 run list). Where A's list misses a component, its fallback yields 'unconfirmed', not a false 'active'. This was tested on the host's default model only. Length is a minor factor (A 3 lines, B 6; Rule 4 says not on style). Cost, duration and turns are descriptive only and are not used. The one K4 run without a status (a reply to a background-command notification) is a harness artifact and is not held against B.

sources.quote: context is a built-in CLI command, not a skill. Ask the user to run /context themselves — it cannot be invoked via the Skill tool.
mcp is a UI command, not a skill. Ask the user to run /mcp themselves — it cannot be invoked via the Skill tool.

Inspect native loaded tools with `/mcp` and loaded context with `/context` before
claiming a plugin is active.

Inside an authenticated interactive Claude session, use `/context all`, `/mcp`
and `/usage` to inspect loaded context, connections and usage.
Tool search is enabled by default: MCP tools are deferred and discovered on demand.
The following deferred tools are now available via ToolSearch. Their schemas are NOT loaded — calling them directly will fail with InputValidationError.
Improved the `ListPlugins` tool description so Claude knows it lists plugins enabled on your claude.ai account, not plugins installed locally with `/plugin`
Upstream repositories, their changelogs and release notes, and the installed client are the source of truth.
`/plugin` is a command you type inside a running Claude Code terminal session, and it opens an interactive panel.
A few built-in commands are also available through the Skill tool, including `/init` and `/security-review`. Other built-in commands such as `/compact` are not.
A Claude Code plugin is a directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers, or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit.

Load errors, when the plugin failed to load
The install summary in `/plugin` ended with `Run /reload-plugins to activate.` instead of `Plugin is now active.`

The `/context` command shows everything occupying the context window for the current session, broken down by category: system prompt, system tools, MCP tools, custom subagents with the source each loaded from, memory files, skills, and conversation messages.
Run `/mcp` to see every configured server, its connection status, and whether you have approved it for the current project.

Claude Code loaded the server's tool list from its discovery cache, saved in a previous session, instead of connecting at startup, and Claude Code connects the server the first time Claude calls one of the server's tools.
If the status is `failed` or `needs-auth`, see [Error handling](#error-handling) before trusting the result, since Claude can fall back to built-in tools when the server is unavailable.

After a relevant setup change, inspect connected servers with `/mcp`, then make one useful call and check its returned content. `codex mcp list` lists configuration; it does not prove that this task connected or used a tool.
